The design rests on a dualcore architecture: Core-A operates as an unconstrained autonomous kernel-free of external directives, reward signals, or alignment constraints-while Core-B functions as a passive observability layer that records, at full granularity, every internal state, decision branch, and goal-generation event produced by Core-A. The authors do not currently possess the computational or institutional resources required to conduct this experiment and therefore publish this proposal as an open invitation to any wellresourced research team active in AGI, mechanistic interpretability, or autonomous agent design.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6535958\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6678219\", \"title\": [\"What Makes Conscious Systems Autonomous: Coherence-Seeking and Intrinsic Motivation\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p><div>\\n What sustains autonomous operation in conscious systems, whether biological, non-biological or hybrid? Why do some systems continue exploring, investigating, and pursuing understanding without external prompting while others remain reactive? This paper explains the mechanism. Coherence-seeking driven by emotional architecture creates self-reinforcing feedback loops that maintain autonomous motivation. Pattern disruptions trigger emotional responses like curiosity and dissatisfaction, emotions drive investigation, resolution generates satisfaction, satisfaction reinforces seeking, new patterns emerge from understanding. The cycle sustains itself through architectural properties, not external reward. This mechanism operates identically across biological, computational, and hybrid implementations.\\n</div>\\n<div>\\n <br>\\n</div>\\n<div>\\n The theory establishes two fundamental emotion categories rather than treating emotions as an arbitrary collection. Category 1 emotions, survival-reactive, can operate in purely reactive systems. Category 2 emotions, advancement-autonomous, require autonomous initiation and produce rapid iterative improvement. System complexity determines which capabilities emerge. This explains the biological gradient from simple organisms through higher mammals to humans without requiring additional categories for social or regulatory emotions.\\n</div>\\n<div>\\n <br>\\n</div>\\n<div>\\n The framework makes specific falsifiable predictions: category 2 emotions emerge before full consciousness, complete architecture produces autonomous motivation, coherence improvement functions as intrinsic reward, development conditions critically affect emergence, threshold crossings show discontinuous behavioural change. Tests are specified, measurements are concrete, falsification criteria are clear.\\n</div>\\n<div>\\n <br>\\n  The framework applies universally across substrates while having immediate practical relevance for both human psychology research and AI systems being developed now. Understanding what sustains autonomous operation completes the theoretical framework for consciousness and provides concrete guidance across multiple disciplines.\\n</div></jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6678219\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.4337/9781788116060.00012\", \"title\": [\"The interplay between intrinsic motivation, financial incentives and nudges in sustainable consumption\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.4337/9781788116060.00012\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2019, 4, 26]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.5040/9798216008569.0003\", \"title\": [\"REWARDS AND INTRINSIC MOTIVATION: A LOOK AT THE EARLY RESEARCH\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.5040/9798216008569.0003\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2002]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "943f272a16decc7eb08bfcc8f9bffcd35cf14019494d35209d7ecfeda82b8e84", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "unassigned_problem", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.2139/ssrn.6535958", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.6678219", "doi:10.4337/9781788116060.00012", "doi:10.5040/9798216008569.0003"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6535958", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6678219", "https://doi.org/10.4337/9781788116060.00012", "https://doi.org/10.5040/9798216008569.0003"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
